params.place: on the map: South Africa, the gap in its middle

moments.what: South Africa's border traces in light round its flag
the trace runs on round the coast
a gap in its middle flashes
the camera pushes in on the gap

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Why does South Africa have a hole in the middle?

params.place: on the map: the gap in South Africa, close

moments.what: the gap pulses
the gap's border traces round
Lesotho's flag fills the gap and LESOTHO writes across it

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: That hole is a country, Lesotho.

params.place: on the map: Lesotho's border posts, Belgium laid beside it for scale

moments.what: a sign on Lesotho shows its area
the area on the sign counts up to its figure
the sign settles with a bump
Belgium's shape slides in beside Lesotho, the same size
roads draw out from the capital
border gates pop where each road crosses
every road ends inside South Africa

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: A whole kingdom of 30,355 km², about as big as Belgium, and every road out of it crosses into South Africa.

params.place: on the map: Thaba Bosiu, a flat mountain in the Caledon valley

moments.what: a chief in a top hat steps onto the map
MOSHOESHOE labels him
his people walk up behind him
a flat-topped mountain rises under them
THABA BOSIU writes on it
raiders climb at its foot
they slide back down the cliffs

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It began with a chief called Moshoeshoe, who led his people up Thaba Bosiu, a flat-topped mountain no army could take.

params.place: on the map: the valleys west of the mountains

moments.what: the camera pulls back from the mountain
small groups walk in from every side
huts pop up across the land
more huts land far apart
a blue colour spreads over all their land
BASOTHO writes across it
fields of maize stripe the valleys
the camera glides west over the fields
the land west of the river glows

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: From that fortress he gathered clans scattered by war into one nation, the Basotho, farming the wide valleys to the west.

params.place: on the map: the Orange Free State, west of the Caledon River

moments.what: BOERS labels the settlers
settlers walk in from the south-west
an ox wagon rolls up behind them
a flag is planted at Bloemfontein
an orange colour spreads east from it
ORANGE FREE STATE writes on it
the valleys flash
the valleys glow gold
dust puffs behind the settlers
the orange edge flashes against the Basotho blue

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: But who else wanted those valleys? Boer settlers, who rolled in by ox wagon and founded the Orange Free State right on top of them.

params.place: on the map: the lowlands between Bloemfontein and the mountains

moments.what: crossed spears stamp on the border
horsemen ride east
orange sweeps over the fields
the maize fields turn orange
the blue shrinks east
the blue stops at the mountains and peaks rise along its edge

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: War after war, the Boers took the farmland, and the Basotho were pushed back toward the mountains.

params.place: on the map: Thaba Bosiu, a letter sailing to Britain

moments.what: a question mark pulses over the last blue land
Moshoeshoe stands on his mountain
he holds up a letter
the letter flies off the top of the map toward Britain
a British flag drops onto the land
the orange stops moving
the remaining land glows
BASUTOLAND writes across it

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So how did any of it survive? Moshoeshoe asked Britain to protect what was left, and his land became Basutoland.

params.place: on the map: the Caledon River along the north-west border

moments.what: the camera slides to the river
a treaty paper unrolls on the map
a giant pen starts drawing
the pen draws the border line
the river glows blue under the line
CALEDON RIVER writes along it
the line closes round the land
today's border traces in light

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Then a treaty drew its north-west border down the Caledon River, where it still runs today.

params.place: on the map: the four colonies around Basutoland

moments.what: the camera pulls back over the whole region
a British flag stands on each colony
four colonies light up, each a different colour
their names pop round the edge
the four colours flow together
one colour fills them all
South Africa's flag fills it
Basutoland stays apart, its border flashing
a gap opens round it

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Decades later, the British colonies all around it joined into one country, South Africa. Basutoland stayed out.

params.place: on the map: Lesotho's mountains, the border all round

moments.what: the camera pushes back in
a crown drops onto the land
the British flag lifts away
Lesotho's flag fills the land
peaks rise across it
South Africa's colour glows round it
arrows point in from every side
the border flashes all the way round

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: In the end it became the independent Kingdom of Lesotho, a country of mountains with South Africa on every side.

params.place: on the map: the Orange River leaving Lesotho, its lowest point

moments.what: the peaks on Lesotho glint
Lesotho's border glows
Lesotho lifts off the map on its mountains
its shadow falls on South Africa
a pin drops where the river leaves
a height post rises from the pin
the post's sign shows the height
the height on the sign counts up as the post's marks light
the post grows taller
a SEA sign glows on the coast
the camera pulls back over the raised country
the sea sign pulses, low on the coast
Lesotho's border flashes, highest of all

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And the Basotho kept only the high ground: the lowest point in Lesotho is 1,400 m above the sea, higher than any other country's lowest point.

params.place: on the map: back over South Africa

moments.what: a mountain peak pops on the left
a British flag pops on the right
both glow over the map
a comment bubble pops between them
the camera pulls back over South Africa
the gap in its middle flashes

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Mountains or the British: which really saved it? Tell me. And next time someone asks you,
